claims.text: SEAL_FILE constant defines the seal filename ".seal.json"; sealPath() joins it under the memory dir.

sealFile(file, home) is the writer that hashes a file's on-disk content and persists it into the seal map via writeSeal (atomic tmp+rename write to .seal.json); sealContent(key, content, home) is a sibling writer that seals content directly by key.
digest(content) computes the sha256 hex digest used as the seal value for a file's content.

checkSeal(file, content, home) is the function that detects out-of-band modification: it compares the current digest against the stored seal entry and returns "diverged" when they differ, "unsealed" (and seals silently) when there is no prior entry, and "sealed" when they match. SealStatus type and DIVERGED_BODY message are defined in the same file.
SealStatus type is "sealed" | "unsealed" | "diverged"; DIVERGED_BODY is the user-facing blocked message shown when a seal has diverged.
memory-seal.ts defines checkSeal, SealStatus, DIVERGED_BODY (src/memory-seal.ts:24-25, 98-116, 117)
src/memory-store.ts is the sole importer of checkSeal/DIVERGED_BODY/sealContent/sealFile/sealKey (src/memory-store.ts:6)

memorySnapshot (src/memory-store.ts, readSealed at L263-274 and memorySnapshot at L501-538) replaces diverged content with DIVERGED_BODY and records an incident, but the write-refusal function (likely memoryAdd) has not yet been located due to a blocked read
